title: Certificates of Deposit: crediting back a penalty charged on a grace-period withdrawal
content:
## Situation this policy governs

Money taken out of a Certificates of Deposit certificate during its grace period carries no penalty, whatever withdrawal kind the entry was recorded under. A penalty charged on such a withdrawal was therefore assessed contrary to the charter, and it is reversed with the adjustment reason bank error.

The business result governed by this policy is the amount credited back to the certificate. The credit is booked with the tool described below and shows at once in the certificate's activity and as a higher principal balance.

## Tool: reverse_grace_penalty_e6d62385

### What it does

The tool credits back to a certificate of deposit a penalty that was charged on money taken out during a grace period. It posts one penalty reversal entry on the certificate, dated today, that points to the penalty entry being credited back and carries the adjustment reason bank_error. The amount is added to the certificate's principal balance at once, so the owner sees the credit in the certificate's activity and a higher principal balance right away. Nothing else about the certificate changes.

### How it is invoked

The agent performs reverse_grace_penalty_e6d62385 as an internal tool, which must first be unlocked and is then called.

### Parameters

- **certificate_id** (identifier): the certificate reference number of the certificate that carries the penalty, as returned by the certificate lookup for this customer.
- **source_item_id** (identifier): the entry reference number of the penalty entry being credited back, as returned by the certificate activity lookup.
- **amount** (USD, 2 decimal places, a positive number rounded half up to the cent): the amount credited back to principal.

### What it returns

A successful call returns a receipt, rendered as text, carrying:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| reversal_id | Entry reference number of the new penalty reversal entry |
| certificate_id | The certificate credited |
| source_item_id | The penalty entry credited back |
| amount | USD credited, 2 decimal places |
| posted_date | Today, YYYY-MM-DD |
| principal_balance | The certificate's new principal in USD, 2 decimal places |

A receipt carrying a reversal_id means the credit is posted.

## Contract questions

**Does the tool check that the withdrawal was in grace?**
No. It posts the reversal with the values supplied; whether the penalty is to be reversed is a matter of policy.

**What reason does the entry carry?**
Always bank_error.
